次日网络流量需求分析与容量规划

A lightweight adaptive multiscale forecasting model was developed to account for short-term fluctuations and long-term trends in hourly backbone network traffic forecasting. Historical windows were represented at three temporal resolutions, and independent decomposition linear experts generated candidate forecasts. A routing network extracted four statistics from the current window: the mean, standard deviation, mean at the last time step, and mean absolute first difference. A multilayer perceptron with two fully connected layers used these statistics to calculate fusion weights. Experiments on Abilene and GÉANT used 96 historical steps to predict the next 24 steps. Across three common random seeds, the proposed method reduced mean squared error by 4.07% and 4.54% relative to the single-scale decomposition linear model, respectively. The corresponding reductions relative to the sampling-oriented lightweight model LightTS were 29.80% and 46.89%. Further ablation experiments across eight random seeds compared the proposed method with learned global weights and a constant-input router. On Abilene, the mean seed-wise improvements over both controls were approximately 1.80%; on GÉANT, they were 4.31% and 4.97%, respectively. The results show that combining multiscale candidate forecasts with low-dimensional routing achieves lower mean forecasting errors with few additional fusion parameters. The forecasts can provide a reference for next-day network traffic demand analysis and capacity planning.

本文结合独立分解线性专家与基于窗口统计特征的尺度路由网络，采用自适应多尺度加权协调各尺度输出，以较小参数规模完成小时级骨干网流量预测。重复实验在两套数据上得到的平均误差均低于所设单尺度与固定融合对照，预测输出可作为未来一天需求分析的参考。后续
在更多网络数据和预测长度下检验模型适用性。
